descriptor.scene: There is no human being in this frame and no second capped mascot figure. The camera is well back and high, looking down across the working floor of the glowing machine, and the PLACE is the subject. A dozen small rounded cream machines run at once across that floor, each on its own piece of work, spaced apart and all plainly busy: hum lines rising, small dials lit amber, short brass rails and chutes threading between them so the floor reads as one connected system rather than a row of objects. Some pieces travel on carriages; one carriage waits at a lowered honey-wood gate; one machine's tray holds a piece that has come back wrong and sits apart from the rest. The manager stands at a vantage in the UPPER LEFT of the frame, on a small honey-wood balcony above the floor, at full length and no taller than a third of the frame height, turned three-quarter with one mitten arm raised and extended out over the machines he commands, head up, weight forward. His plum light reaches down across the whole floor. Warm honeyed and cream light. Composition: balcony and manager upper left, the dozen machines filling the middle and the right; the lower left of the frame stays calm lit floor.
descriptor._caption: The way through is never a straight line. A dozen machines run at once, each on its own piece, and he holds the order in his head: what can start now, what must wait, what to do when a piece comes back wrong.
negatives: a human being of any kind
the manager down on the floor working a machine with his own body
